questions.q: Why had Toad been put in prison?
choices: For stealing a motor-car and being rude to policemen
For not paying his taxes
For fighting with the weasels
For breaking into a farmhouse
questions.evidence: imprisoned so justly for stealing so handsome a motor-car

questions.q: How did Toad behave during his first weeks in the dungeon?
choices: He wept, despaired and refused his meals
He cheerfully planned his escape
He made friends with all the guards
He wrote letters to his lawyers every day
questions.evidence: refusing his meals or intermediate light refreshments

questions.q: Why did the gaoler's daughter ask to look after Toad?
choices: She was fond of animals and pitied his misery
Her father ordered her to guard him
She wanted to be paid by Toad
She hoped to marry a rich toad
questions.evidence: I can't bear to see that poor beast so unhappy

questions.q: What finally made Toad sit up, dry his eyes and start eating?
choices: Hot buttered toast and tea
A letter from Badger
A visit from Rat and Mole
A bowl of bread-and-water
questions.evidence: The smell of that buttered toast simply talked to Toad

questions.q: Toad ate the toast "with avidity." What does "avidity" mean?
choices: Great eagerness
Slow carefulness
Sadness
Disgust
questions.evidence: pitching into the toast with avidity

questions.q: When the girl asked about Toad Hall, why did she laugh and say "I don't want to TAKE it"?
choices: Toad described it like an advertisement for selling a house
Toad offered to give her the house
Toad said the house was falling down
Toad refused to talk about it
questions.evidence: Five minutes from church, post-office, and golf-links

questions.q: Why did the girl NOT tell Toad that she was fond of animals as pets?
choices: She knew it would greatly offend him
She was afraid of her father
She did not really like animals
She wanted to keep him as a pet secretly

questions.q: What was the girl's plan for Toad's escape?
choices: Toad would dress as her aunt, the washerwoman, and walk out
Toad would dig a tunnel under the wall
Toad would hide in a laundry basket
Her father would let him out at night
questions.evidence: you could escape from the castle as the official washerwoman

questions.q: How did Toad first respond to the idea of dressing as a washerwoman?
choices: He was proud and huffy and thought it beneath him
He thanked her and agreed at once
He laughed and said it was a clever idea
He cried because he was afraid
questions.evidence: going about the country disguised as a washerwoman

questions.q: What did the washerwoman ask for besides Toad's money?
choices: To be gagged, bound and left in a corner
To be given Toad's coat and waistcoat
A ride home in a motor-car
A job at Toad Hall
questions.evidence: she should be gagged and bound and dumped down in a corner

questions.q: The washerwoman's plan used a "not very convincing artifice." What is an "artifice"?
choices: A clever trick meant to fool people
A kind of clothing
A prison guard
A large key
questions.evidence: By this not very convincing artifice

questions.q: What problem did Toad discover at the railway booking-office?
choices: He had left his money in his waistcoat back in the cell
The train had already left
The clerk recognized him as Toad
There were no trains going toward his home
questions.evidence: he had left both coat and waistcoat behind him in his cell

questions.q: What did the engine-driver ask Toad to do in return for a ride?
choices: Wash some of his shirts
Shovel coal on the engine
Pay him later from Toad Hall
Cook him supper
questions.evidence: If you'll wash a few shirts for me when you get home

questions.q: What does the chapter tell us about Toad's real plans for the engine-driver's shirts?
choices: He never meant to wash them and planned to send money instead
He planned to wash them carefully himself
He would ask the gaoler's daughter to wash them
He planned to throw them away
questions.evidence: he had never washed a shirt in his life

questions.q: What did the engine-driver notice after they had traveled many miles?
choices: Another engine full of police and warders was chasing them
The train was running out of coal
A tree had fallen across the rails
Toad had fallen asleep
questions.evidence: It looks as if we were being pursued!

questions.q: Why did the engine-driver decide to help Toad even after hearing the truth?
choices: He disliked motor-cars and being ordered about by policemen, and felt sorry for Toad
Toad promised him a fortune
He was afraid of Toad
He did not believe Toad's story
questions.evidence: I don't hold with motor-cars, for one thing

questions.q: How did Toad escape the pursuing engine?
choices: He jumped from the train after a tunnel and hid in a wood
He hid under a pile of coal
He jumped into a river
He climbed onto the roof of a carriage
questions.evidence: Toad jumped, rolled down a short embankment

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Toad escapes from prison disguised as a washerwoman and flees by train
Toad wins his case in court and goes home
Rat and Mole break Toad out of prison
Toad buys a railway engine
